name: PA-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean of about 15 points on the partisan voting index
Incumbent Mary Gay Scanlon seeking re-election with a large financial advantage
Republican challenger has raised under $10,000 with no outside spending support
Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 98%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Scanlon: a +15 Democratic district, incumbency, and a lopsided money edge of roughly $990,000 raised versus under $10,000 for her challenger, with no outside spending to close the gap. Markets agree, pricing her near 98%, so the forecast stays at a Safe D with a margin in the low twenties.
model.watch: Any late surge of outside Republican spending or an unexpected polling miss in the Philadelphia suburbs would be the main signal to revisit this rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Incumbent Mary Gay Scanlon (D) is running.

overview:
Mary Gay Scanlon defends a Delaware County-area seat that leans about 15 points Democratic, and she is running for re-election as the incumbent. Her challenger, Nicholas Manganaro, has run a minimal campaign, raising under $10,000 with no outside groups involved on either side.

Scanlon has raised nearly $1 million and holds about $450,000 on hand, giving her an overwhelming resource advantage. Prediction markets price her chances near 98%, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the outlook rests on the district's lean, her incumbency, and the fundraising gap, all of which point to a comfortable Democratic hold.
